newsitem.title: USA: Colombia files shelf for $1 billion in debt.
newsitem.headline: Colombia files shelf for $1 billion in debt.

text.p: The Republic of Colombia said Wednesday it filed a shelf registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to $1 billion in debt securities and warrants to purchase debt securities.
When combined with a previous registration, Colombia will have a total $1.325 billion in debt securities available for sale, the filing said.
The proceeds will be used by the government for general budgetary purposes, the filing said.
Colombia also filed a registration to sell up to $750 million in bonds due February 2007, the filing said.
The offering will be made through Merrill Lynch & Co and J.P. Morgan & Co. Application has been made to list the bonds on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
Proceeds from the sale of the bonds will also be used for general budgetary purposes, the filing said.
